introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0595 COMPUTER SCIENCE 1, June 2021, Ordinary Level. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones and calculators are NOT allowed in the examination room. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: decide which answer is correct and mark only one answer for each question (if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Calculators are NOT allowed. Do all rough work in the question booklet.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 1 to 50 are independent; all carry equal marks.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following software does not display graphics?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **text editor** (such as Notepad) works only with plain characters: it has no tools to insert pictures, shapes or charts. A word processor can insert images and drawings, a desktop publishing package is built around page layout with graphics, and presentation software is made of slides full of pictures and charts. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The correct arrangement in increasing order of time unit is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Each unit is 1000 times bigger than the one before it: $1\ \text{ps} = 10^{-12}\ \text{s}$, $1\ \text{ns} = 10^{-9}\ \text{s}$, $1\ \mu\text{s} = 10^{-6}\ \text{s}$. So the increasing order is picoseconds, nanoseconds, microseconds. Options A, B and C each put one unit in the wrong place. Option D is the right order (the printed option contains a stray extra comma). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ______ deals with the design of equipment and the workplace to ensure safety and comfort.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Ergonomics** is the study of how to design equipment, furniture and the working environment (chair height, screen position, lighting) so that people work safely and comfortably. Biometrics identifies people from body features, and modelling builds a representation of a system. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Having unauthorized access to a computer system and collecting sensitive data from it is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Breaking into a computer system without permission in order to steal or collect data is **cracking** (illegal hacking). Copyright is the legal protection of an author's work, plagiarism is copying someone's work and presenting it as your own, and bridging is a networking term. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following has the fastest access speed?
questions.corrige_markdown: Memory speed decreases as we move away from the processor: registers (inside the CPU) are faster than RAM, which is faster than the hard drive, which is faster than optical discs (CD/DVD). The fastest of the four is therefore the **registers**. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The file extension .avi holds what type of files?
questions.corrige_markdown: AVI (Audio Video Interleave) is a **video** file format. Sound files use extensions such as .mp3 or .wav, graphics .jpg or .png, and text files .txt or .docx. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One application of infrared signals is in ______
questions.corrige_markdown: Infrared signals are used over short distances and in line of sight, for example in the **remote controller** of a television. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi wireless networks use radio waves, and traffic lights use visible light from lamps, not infrared data signals. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The health concern RSI stands for?
questions.corrige_markdown: RSI is the abbreviation of **Repetitive Strain Injury**: damage to muscles, tendons or nerves (for example in the wrist) caused by repeating the same movement, such as typing or using a mouse for long periods. The other options change a word ("Repeated", "Stress") or contain a spelling error ("Injure"). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What characteristic of RAM makes it not suitable for permanent storage?
questions.corrige_markdown: RAM is **volatile**: it loses all its contents when the power is switched off, so it cannot keep data permanently. RAM is actually very fast (A is false), and being the main memory or being used by the CPU are not reasons why it cannot store data permanently. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It is often in use by the CPU

questions.enonce_markdown: When a computer is switch on, the operating system is loaded in a process called
questions.corrige_markdown: **Booting** (starting up) is the process in which the bootstrap program loads the operating system from the disk into memory when the computer is switched on. Compiling translates a program, formatting prepares a disk, and debugging removes errors from a program. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main use of defragmentation utility program is to
questions.corrige_markdown: Over time the pieces of a file are scattered over the disk (fragmentation), so the read head must jump around. A defragmentation utility rearranges the pieces so that each file is stored in contiguous sectors, which **reduces data access time**. It does not delete files (C), does not create more space in any real sense (B) and has nothing to do with viruses (D, an antivirus job). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Delete any unused data and files

questions.enonce_markdown: Software is said to be user friendly if:
questions.corrige_markdown: User-friendly software is **easy to learn and easy to use**, even for a beginner. Making friends, being usable for other things, or containing many pictures are not the definition. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It is easy to use and make friends
It is easy to learn and use
The user can use it for other things

questions.enonce_markdown: The result of the binary operation 1101-1010 is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Convert to decimal: $1101_2 = 13$ and $1010_2 = 10$, so $13 - 10 = 3 = 011_2$ (in three bits). Direct subtraction column by column gives the same result: $1101 - 1010 = 0011$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An application software designed to perform a wide range of tasks and can be used by a variety of users is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown: **Generic software** (general-purpose software) such as a word processor or a spreadsheet can do many different tasks and is sold to many users. Specialized or bespoke (custom-made) software is written for one particular task or customer, and integrated software is a package that combines several applications. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A data type in which data items can only have one of two possible values is a(n)
questions.corrige_markdown: A **Boolean** data item can be only TRUE or FALSE (1 or 0). A string is a sequence of characters, an array is a collection of items of the same type, and a record groups items of different types. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A communication mode where data is transmitted in one direction at a time is referred to as:

*Options as printed:* A) Simplex   B) Duplex   C) Half duplex   D) Half simplex
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **half duplex** mode, data can travel in both directions along the link, but only one direction at a time (a walkie-talkie is an example). In simplex mode data travels in one fixed direction only (television broadcast), in duplex (full duplex) mode both directions are used at the same time (telephone), and "half simplex" is not a standard mode.

**Intended answer: C (Half duplex).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A collection of rules for the transmission of signals across networks is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **protocol** is a set of rules that governs how data is formatted, sent and received on a network (for example TCP/IP or HTTP). A topology is the layout of a network and hypertext is linked text. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Input, processing, output and storage are collectively referred to as the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The four stages through which data passes in a computer form the **information processing cycle**: input, processing, output and storage. The other names are not standard terms. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a database?
questions.corrige_markdown: A database is an organised collection of related data that can be searched and managed. An address book, a telephone directory and a class list are all organised collections of records. A **list of only 3 names** is too small and has no structure (no fields, no records), so it is the odd one out. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: A class list of form 5 students

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following means the same thing as a row of data in a relation or table in a database is?
questions.corrige_markdown: In relational database terms a row of a table is called a **tuple** (also called a record). Attributes (fields) are the columns, and a file is the whole table stored on disk. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to a column in a relation or table in a database?
questions.corrige_markdown: A column of a relation holds one kind of data for every row and is called an **attribute** (or field). A tuple is a row, an entity is the thing described by the table, and a file is the whole table stored on disk. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of the computers to create, store, revise and produce text is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Using a computer to create, store, edit (revise) and print text is **word processing**. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A device capable of converting analog signal to digital signal and vice versa:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **modem** (modulator-demodulator) converts the digital signals of a computer into analog signals for transmission over a telephone line (modulation) and converts incoming analog signals back to digital (demodulation). A multiplexer combines several signals on one line and a coaxial cable is only a transmission medium. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A company network that allows only controlled access from the outside and for specific purposes is called
questions.corrige_markdown: An **extranet** is a private company network (an intranet) that is opened in a controlled way to selected outsiders such as suppliers or customers. The Internet is public, an intranet is for the company's own staff only, and a firewall is a security device, not a type of network. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A logic gate whose functionality is the reverse of an OR gate is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The reverse (inverse) of OR is **NOR** (NOT-OR): its output is the opposite of the output of OR for every input. Truth table for inputs (A,B) = 00, 01, 10, 11: OR gives 0, 1, 1, 1 and NOR gives 1, 0, 0, 0. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many combinations of input values in a two- input OR gate result in an output of 1?
questions.corrige_markdown: A two-input gate has $2^2 = 4$ input combinations: 00, 01, 10, 11. The OR gate outputs 0 only for 00 and outputs 1 for the other **3** combinations (01, 10, 11). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The binary equivalent of the decimal 133 is
questions.corrige_markdown: $133 = 128 + 4 + 1 = 2^7 + 2^2 + 2^0$, so the bits for 128, 4 and 1 are 1 and all the others are 0: $10000101_2$. Check: $128 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 133$. Option B is 197, C is 153 and D is 229. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In a flow chart, the symbol below represents:

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In a flowchart the **parallelogram** is the input/output symbol: it is used for reading data in (INPUT) and for displaying results (PRINT). Of the four options, only "an output" matches this symbol. A decision is a diamond, a process is a rectangle and start/stop is a rounded box (terminator). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A printer whose printing mechanism involves pressing the characters against an inked ribbon on to a paper is:
questions.corrige_markdown: An **impact printer** (dot-matrix, daisy-wheel) physically strikes an inked ribbon against the paper. Inkjet and laser printers are non-impact printers: they spray ink or use toner and a laser without striking the paper. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ______ is a transmission mode in which data is transmitted one bit at a time.
questions.corrige_markdown: In **serial transmission** the bits are sent one after another along a single channel. In parallel transmission several bits (for example 8) are sent at the same time on separate wires. Duplex and half duplex describe the direction of the flow, not how many bits are sent at once. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following network topologies uses a token?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **ring topology** (token ring) a special message called a token travels round the ring and only the device holding the token may transmit, which avoids collisions. Mesh, bus and star networks do not use a token. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A network hardware device that connects two dissimilar networks is a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **router** connects different networks (for example a LAN and the Internet) and forwards packets between them. A bridge joins two segments of the same type of network, a hub only repeats signals inside one LAN, and a modem converts signals between analog and digital. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Computers in offices in the school administrative block are connected so they can share resources. What type of network is most likely used?
questions.corrige_markdown: Computers in the offices of one block form a network over a small area, which is a **LAN** (Local Area Network). A PAN covers a person's own devices, a MAN a city and a WAN a very large area such as a country. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A hard disk in divided into tracks which are further divided into:
questions.corrige_markdown: The surface of a hard disk is divided into concentric circles called tracks, and each track is divided into **sectors**, the smallest units of storage that can be read or written. Heads are the parts that read the disk, and clusters are groups of sectors used by the file system. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The performance of a computer system is affected by all except:
questions.corrige_markdown: The speed of the processor (clock speed), the amount of RAM and the size and speed of the hard disk all influence how fast a computer system works. The **power rating** (electrical power consumed) does not measure performance. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 36 to 38 are based on the following algorithm:

```text
1. Start
2. Input x
3. If (x mod 2 = 0) then
   3.1 Set y to x
   3.2 Set counter to 1
   3.3 While counter <= 3 do
         Set y to y+2
         Increment counter by 1
       Endwhile
   3.4 print y
   Else
   3.5 print x
   Endif
4. Stop
```

In what form has the algorithm been represented?
questions.corrige_markdown: The algorithm is written as numbered English-like statements (Input, Set, While ... do, Endwhile, Endif) that follow programming-style structure without the exact syntax of a language. This is **pseudocode**. A flowchart uses symbols, source code uses a real language such as C or Pascal, and machine code is binary. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 36 to 38 are based on the following algorithm:

```text
1. Start
2. Input x
3. If (x mod 2 = 0) then
   3.1 Set y to x
   3.2 Set counter to 1
   3.3 While counter <= 3 do
         Set y to y+2
         Increment counter by 1
       Endwhile
   3.4 print y
   Else
   3.5 print x
   Endif
4. Stop
```

What construct is used in line 3.3?
questions.corrige_markdown: Line 3.3 is `While counter <= 3 do ... Endwhile`: a block of instructions is repeated while a condition is true. This is a **loop** (iteration). The selection construct is the `If ... then ... Else ... Endif` in line 3. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 36 to 38 are based on the following algorithm:

```text
1. Start
2. Input x
3. If (x mod 2 = 0) then
   3.1 Set y to x
   3.2 Set counter to 1
   3.3 While counter <= 3 do
         Set y to y+2
         Increment counter by 1
       Endwhile
   3.4 print y
   Else
   3.5 print x
   Endif
4. Stop
```

What value of y is printed when x is 4?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trace with $x = 4$: $4 \bmod 2 = 0$, so the `If` branch runs. $y = 4$, counter $= 1$. The loop runs while counter $\le 3$:

| Pass | counter before | y after | counter after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 6 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 8 | 3 |
| 3 | 3 | 10 | 4 |

When counter is 4 the condition is false, so the loop stops and `print y` displays **10** (the loop adds 2 three times: $4 + 3 \times 2 = 10$). Verified with a Python simulation. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The input to a compiler is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A compiler translates a program written in a high-level language, the **source code**, into object (machine) code. Object code is the output of the compiler, not its input. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A communication medium in which messages are transmitted as light pulses.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Optic fibre** carries data as pulses of light through thin glass or plastic strands. Coaxial and twisted-pair cables carry electrical signals, and the system bus is inside the computer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ______ enables a wireless network to be connected to a wired network.
questions.corrige_markdown: A wireless **access point** receives and sends radio signals from wireless devices and is itself plugged into the wired network (through a cable), so it links the wireless network to the wired one. A hub and a switch connect wired devices, and a network interface card connects one computer to a network. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A barcode reader is an example of ______ input technology.

*Options as printed:* A) OCR   B) OMR   C) MICR   D) Biometric
questions.corrige_markdown:
A barcode reader shines a light beam over a pattern of dark and light bars and reads the reflected light, so it is an **optical** input technology: it belongs to the family of optical readers together with OCR (optical character recognition, which reads printed characters) and OMR (optical mark recognition, which reads pencil marks on forms). MICR reads characters printed in magnetic ink (bank cheques) and biometric devices read body features (fingerprint, face). None of the four printed options names barcode reading exactly, so the intended answer is the word that completes the sentence, "optical", and the closest printed options are the optical ones (A or B).

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Uploading and downloading data to or from a remote computer is done using?
questions.corrige_markdown: **File Transfer Protocol (FTP)** is the Internet service designed to upload files to, and download files from, a remote computer (server). Internet Relay Chat is for online chat, a download manager only speeds up downloads, and data transmission is a general term. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A technique of developing a miniature of a system with all functional components is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Prototyping** means building a small working model (a miniature) of the system with its main functions, which users can test before the full system is built. The systems development life cycle is the whole sequence of stages, stepwise refinement breaks a problem into smaller steps, and modelling represents a system without necessarily building it. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a PERT chart, tasks are represented using:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) network diagram, the **arrows** represent the tasks (activities) and carry their duration, while the nodes (circles) represent the events, that is the start and end points of tasks. Numbers and letters are only labels. (A dummy task is the dotted arrow used to show a dependency, see question 46.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A task that must be completed before another task can begin is called a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A task that has to be finished before another one can start is the **predecessor** of that task. A dummy task only shows a dependency and takes no time, a milestone marks an important point in a project, and a critical task is one on the critical path whose delay delays the whole project. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these software is suitable for storing, retrieving and manipulating very large quantities of data?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **Database Management System (DBMS)** is designed to store very large amounts of data, to retrieve it quickly with queries and to update it. A spreadsheet is suited to calculations on a limited amount of data. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: On typing a document, instead of typing 456 the typist types 457. What kind of error is this?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **transcription error** is a mistake made when copying or typing data (here one digit is replaced by a wrong one). A transposition error would swap two digits (456 typed as 465). A range check or data type error are checks made by validation, not kinds of typing mistake. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Digital signals are stepwise and discrete while analog signals are:
questions.corrige_markdown: An analog signal varies in a **smooth and continuous** way (like a sound wave), taking any value in a range, while a digital signal jumps between a limited set of values (0 and 1). Square and stepwise shapes describe digital signals. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In computer programming, what is a semantic error?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **semantic error** is a logic error: the instruction is written correctly but it does not do what the programmer intended (a wrong instruction or operation), so the program runs but gives wrong results. An instruction that does not have the right form is a syntax error (D), which the compiler reports (B), and an error during execution is a run-time error (A). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: An error that occurs in the execution of a program
A mistake due to use of the wrong instruction
A mistake due to an instruction not having the right form
